proposed_widenings.name: DamageOnHitOperation.scope (caster_any_weapon_hit)
proposed_widenings.justification: DamageOnHitOperation currently fires 'when the caster hits a creature in the attachment scope' — the attachment IS the hit target (e.g., Hunter's Mark mark). Divine Favor has no specific target: the rider fires on any weapon attack hit by the caster regardless of target. Using self attachment produces a false on_hit_window label ('caster hits self') and routes the damage attaches_to edge to the caster rather than the hit creature. A scope field (or a new attachment kind) is needed to express 'caster-scoped: any weapon hit made by the caster' distinct from 'target-scoped: hit against the specific attached creature'.
proposed_widenings.evidence: "Until the spell ends, your attacks with weapons deal an extra 1d4 Radiant damage on a hit."

notes: The ongoing_effect family fits cleanly and all required v4 atoms exist (on_hit_window, damage, self, spell_slot, bonus_action_quota, persist, expire). The sole gap is the DamageOnHitOperation scope: the existing type assumes the attachment identifies the hit target, but Divine Favor fires on any weapon hit the caster makes. No structural or atom widening is needed — only a surface variant that adds a caster-wide weapon-hit scope.
